sections.label: Parliament scrutiny and accountability
sections.summary: Parliament must ensure the Government stays faithful to its duty, and PQs are the primary means for MPs to scrutinise the Government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As such, I hope the House will agree with me that Parliament, as the primary organ of the Legislative Branch, must not only be able to discharge its law-making responsibilities, but also to ensure that the Government remains faithful to its duty to all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: PQs are a critical aspect of Government accountability, as they are the primary means by which Members of Parliament (MPs) can scrutinise the Government’s performance, as well as to reflect the concerns that are brought to us by our constituents.

sections.label: Consulting MPs on question redirection
sections.summary: The MP asks whether MPs could be consulted on any intended redirection of questions so their input is considered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Moving forward, could MPs be consulted on any intended redirection of questions, so that our input can be taken into account?

sections.label: Cabinet Ministers on PCMR
sections.summary: The MP asks whether there is a conflict of interest in appointing Cabinet Ministers to the PCMR.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Is there not a conflict of interest here?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I must confess to be perplexed as to why Cabinet Ministers need to be appointed to the PCMR.

sections.label: PCMR composition and terms
sections.summary: The MP asks whether the PCMR should instead be non-political distinguished citizens on fixed terms, as the Wee Chong Jin Commission recommended.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Indeed, the PCMR is the only institution I am aware of where some members serve for life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would it thus not be far superior to keep the PCMR as a council of distinguished citizens who are non-political individuals, on fixed terms, as recommended by the Wee Chong Jin Commission?

sections.label: Time between Bill Readings
sections.summary: Bills are introduced at prior Sittings, with generally 10 clear days between First and Second Readings, giving MPs about a month per Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Bills are introduced at prior Sittings and as a general rule, there must be 10 clear days between the First and the Second Readings of a Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Hence, MPs generally have about a month to go through each Bill, which forms the basis of the Minister's Second Reading speech.

sections.label: MAS Minister insurer conditions
sections.summary: The Bill allowed the Minister in-charge of MAS to impose conditions on approval of applications for effective control or substantial shareholding of a licensed insurer involving a co-operative.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The purpose of the Bill was to allow the Minister in-charge of MAS to impose conditions on an approval of an application to obtain effective control or become a substantial shareholder of a licensed insurer where a co-operative is concerned.

sections.label: Certificates of Urgency use
sections.summary: Certificates of Urgency have been and will continue to be used sparingly and only when necessary.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Measures, such as Certificates of Urgency, have been and will continue to be used sparingly and only when necessary.

sections.label: PCMR composition and historical context
sections.summary: Members who remember the historical context of Bills and legislative provisions are valuable, so the speaker sees no objection to the PCMR composition suggested by Ms Lim.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: And it is important to remember, sometimes, that there are Bills which were passed, legislative provisions that were made because of a certain historical context.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Therefore, having people who remember that context, who remember the original situation in which a certain legislative provision was provided or certain reasons why we did not put in legislative provisions, that is valuable and that is useful.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: So, I cannot see any objection to the composition of the PCMR in the terms suggested by Ms Lim.

sections.label: Permanent members and Insurance Bill process
sections.summary: The speaker sees no objection to permanent members and notes the Standing Orders allow an urgent case to skip a Select Committee.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, I do not see the objection to having permanent members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Then the second point on the legislative process and the Insurance (Amendment) Bill, I do take Miss Lim's point that, in the normal case, it would go to a Select Committee.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But the Standing Orders also do provide that in an urgent case, that it need not go to a Select Committee.

sections.label: Urgency of Insurance Amendment Bill
sections.summary: Select Committee proceedings take time, and given market concerns there was urgency to act in this instance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Because when we go to a Select Committee, it takes time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And in this particular instance, given that there were concerns with the market, as I have explained, there was urgency to do it.

sections.label: Filing questions after full answer
sections.summary: Under the Standing Orders, a Member may be precluded from filing a question again if it is deemed fully answered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Just to respond that under the Standing Orders, a Member may be precluded from filing a question again if it is deemed to have been fully answered.

sections.label: Redirecting questions to other Ministries
sections.summary: If a question was meant for another Ministry it was not fully answered, so it can be redirected, and the aborted deal question should go to Minister Edwin Tong.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The first point that Ms Lim made was that because of the Standing Orders, which says that if a question has been answered fully, then you cannot bring it again.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But that is the point, because if the MP felt that this was supposed to have been addressed to another Ministry, it must follow that it was not answered fully, so then they can direct it to the other Ministry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And with respect to the last question, when she raised the issue of the deal being aborted and what the response was, this is a classic example of a question that should not be directed to me.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: That should instead go to Minister Edwin Tong.
